javax.microedition.theme
Class ThemeManager

java.lang.Object
  javax.microedition.theme.ThemeManager

public class ThemeManager
extends java.lang.Object

Provides applications access to themes installed in the device or in the application's JAR file. Using ThemeManager, applications can:

  • Query the system for installed themes
  • Obtain a reference to the currently active theme or any other installed theme, including the system default theme
  • Register to be notified about changes in the theme system (switching the active theme, changes to the customizable elements of the active theme, installations and removals of themes)

If no theme has been explicitly activated, the system default theme remains in effect. It contains a default appearance for all the customizable elements recognized by the implementation, and its elements cannot be modified by applications.

There must be only one instance of ThemeManager in the system. Changes made to themes using ThemeManager affect the whole device.

Notifications about theme-related events are sent asynchronously. The method that causes the event does not need to return before the notification is sent.

Method Detail

activateTheme

public void activateTheme(java.lang.String name)
                   throws ThemeException

Activates a previously installed theme. The theme that was active at the time of this method invocation is implicitly deactivated if the activation of the new theme is successful. However, if the theme being activated is the same as the currently active theme, this method does nothing.

If the activation is successful, this method must dispatch the themeActivated event to all registered listeners.

If the theme data is invalid, or there is an implementation-specific failure, a ThemeException must be thrown.

Parameters:
name - the unique name of the theme to activate
Throws:
ThemeException - if the theme cannot be activated
ThemeNotFoundException - if the theme to activate was not found
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if name is empty, or is not in name:version:vendor format and is not the system default theme
java.lang.NullPointerException - if name is null
java.lang.SecurityException - if the theme to activate is DRM protected but the usage rights have expired

addThemeListener

public void addThemeListener(ThemeListener listener)

Registers a theme listener. Applications that need information about events related to themes (such as the activation and deletion of a theme) need to register with ThemeManager to get notifications of the events. This allows them to react appropriately to appearance changes, for example by repainting a custom component.

Theme listeners must implement the ThemeListener interface.

If the listener has already been registered or null is passed, this method does nothing.

Parameters:
listener - the listener to register
See Also:
ThemeListener

createTheme

public void createTheme(java.lang.String themeLocator,
                        java.lang.String name)
                 throws ThemeException,
                        ModifyNotSupportedException

Creates a theme programmatically from a theme descriptor found using the locator passed as a parameter. If the implementation does not support modify operations, this method must immediately throw ModifyNotSupportedException.

The themeLocator parameter must be a URI. Currently the only protocol type supported is file. This allows applications to construct themes from a JSR 258 compliant appearance descriptor that resides in the file system of the device, along with any media objects it refers to.

If the creation of the theme is successful, the implementation must store it persistently so that it is subsequently available for all applications in the system.

The name parameter must be a theme name string in the form "name:version:vendor", where name, version and vendor correspond to the name, version and vendor attributes, respectively, of some theme element in the descriptor. If the parameter is not formally correct, a java.lang.IllegalArgumentException must be thrown.

Because the theme creation could take considerable time, this method must not block. If the theme creation was successful, this method must dispatch the themeCreated event to registered listeners when the creation is complete.

The newly created theme is not activated by default. Applications need to use the activateTheme method to activate it.

If the theme creation is successful, a themeCreated message is sent to all registered listeners when the creation is complete. If the operation fails before the theme creation is initiated, a ThemeException must be thrown.

Error conditions that must result in a ThemeException being thrown include (but are not limited to) the following:

  • No appearance descriptor found at locator
  • Descriptor not well-formed, or not valid
  • Missing referred media elements
  • Insufficient resources to create theme
  • No definition for theme with given name found in descriptor
  • Theme of specified name already exists

This method must apply the context, element and policy checks as described in the "File Format Reference" section.

Parameters:
themeLocator - the locator for the theme descriptor
name - the name of the theme to create
Throws:
ThemeException - if there was an error creating the theme
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if themeLocator is not a valid URI, or name is empty or not a valid theme name string
java.lang.NullPointerException - if any parameter is null
ModifyNotSupportedException - if the implementation does not support modify operations
java.lang.SecurityException - if the application does not have the permission to manage appearances
See Also:

getTheme

public Theme getTheme(java.lang.String name)
               throws ThemeNotFoundException

Gets the theme with the specified unique name. The name must be a theme name string as defined in the File Format Reference, or the value of the SYSTEM_DEFAULT_THEME constant. The system default theme can only be retrieved using this value.

Parameters:
name - a theme name string, or SYSTEM_DEFAULT_THEME
Returns:
the theme instance
Throws:
ThemeNotFoundException - if the theme is not found
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if name is empty, or is not in name:version:vendor format and is not the system default theme
java.lang.NullPointerException - if name is null

getThemes

public java.lang.String[] getThemes()

Gets the names of all themes installed in the device. The returned array always has at least one element, the reserved name of the system default theme (the value of the SYSTEM_DEFAULT_THEME constant). It must be the first value in the array. Other values, if any, are theme name strings as described in the File Format Reference.

Applications should use the getTheme method with a theme name string from the result array to get an instance of a theme.

Returns:
an array of theme names
See Also:
SYSTEM_DEFAULT_THEME

removeTheme

public void removeTheme(java.lang.String name)
                 throws ThemeException

Removes a theme installed in the device. If the theme was removed successfully, all registered listeners must be sent a themeRemoved event.

The system default theme can not be removed by applications. If an application attempts to remove the system default theme, this method must throw a ThemeException. The system default theme can be identified with the SYSTEM_DEFAULT_THEME constant.

The currently active theme can not be removed by applications. If an application attempts to remove the currently active theme, this method must throw a ThemeException.

Parameters:
name - the unique name of the theme to remove
Throws:
ThemeNotFoundException - if the theme was not found
ThemeException - if there was an error removing the theme or an attempt was made to remove the system default theme
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if name is empty, or is not in name:version:vendor format and is not the system default theme
java.lang.NullPointerException - if name is null
java.lang.SecurityException - if the application does not have the permission to manage appearances

removeThemeListener
